description: Emergency-stop condition is active. On Haas Desktop Mill troubleshooting, the alarm may fail to reset when the primary E-stop cable is disconnected or damaged.
possible_causes: Primary E-stop cable disconnected; E-stop cable damaged; E-stop-related connection/port problem.
official_corrective_action: Check the E-stop cable and its connection. If the cable is undamaged, reconnect it and cycle machine power; if damaged, replace it and power cycle. Follow the applicable Haas service procedure.
source_document: Haas Desktop Mill Troubleshooting Guide TG0058; Haas Alarm Search Help RD0002

description: The compressed air supplied to the machine is below the minimum pressure or flow required.
possible_causes: Insufficient compressed-air pressure or flow; contamination affecting the air-pressure sensor.
official_corrective_action: Check the air supply and pressure. Check the air-pressure sensor for contamination; replace the sensor if required. Haas states that the air supply should be clean and dry.
source_document: Haas NGC Sensors and Switches Service Manual

description: The spindle drive has reported a fault. Haas directs the technician to inspect the spindle-drive error code for the specific cause.
possible_causes: Multiple possible spindle-drive faults; DC-bus problem; vector-drive short circuit; drive or motor/cable fault depending on the machine/control configuration.
official_corrective_action: Read the error code shown on the spindle drive and follow the applicable Haas spindle-drive troubleshooting procedure. Do not assume a single root cause from alarm 123 alone.
source_document: Haas Spindle Drive Troubleshooting Guide TG0133; Haas Vector Drive Troubleshooting Guides

description: The spindle speed is not at zero during a tool change.
possible_causes: Spindle has not stopped before the tool-change operation.
official_corrective_action: Use the Haas diagnostic data and applicable spindle/tool-change troubleshooting procedure to identify why the spindle has not reached zero speed.
source_document: Haas Spindle Drive Troubleshooting Guide TG0133

description: The spindle does not turn when commanded to.
possible_causes: The spindle is not responding to the commanded rotation; the underlying drive, motor, control signal, or mechanical condition must be diagnosed.
official_corrective_action: Use the Haas spindle troubleshooting procedure and diagnostic data to identify why the spindle does not turn. Do not treat the alarm alone as proof of a specific failed component.
source_document: Haas Spindle Drive Troubleshooting Guide TG0133

description: The spindle motor has entered an overload condition.
possible_causes: Internal short circuit; failed temperature sensor; over-aggressive application; shorted vector drive; failed vector-drive fans; incorrect or loose cable connection; shorted spindle motor cable; burnt or shorted Wye/Delta contacts; worn or damaged spindle encoder belt.
official_corrective_action: Follow the Haas spindle-motor troubleshooting procedure for the applicable machine. Inspect/test the spindle motor, overheat sensor, vector drive, fans, cables, Wye/Delta contacts and encoder belt as applicable.
source_document: Haas 30T/40T Spindle Motor Troubleshooting Guide TG0009

description: The spindle motor has reached an overheat condition.
possible_causes: Over-aggressive application; failed spindle fan; spindle-motor temperature-sensor problem.
official_corrective_action: Adjust the machining program/application as appropriate. Check the spindle fan and cable. Inspect the spindle-motor temperature sensor and its cable/connection according to the Haas procedure.
source_document: Haas 30T/40T Spindle Motor Troubleshooting Guide TG0009

description: The control has detected an electronics overheat condition that remains long enough to generate the alarm.
possible_causes: Control-cabinet temperature too high; clogged air filters; cooling fans not operating correctly.
official_corrective_action: Inspect the control cabinet for clogged air filters and correctly operating fans. Follow the applicable Haas electrical/service procedure.
severity: Machine operation inhibited while alarm persists
source_document: Haas Mill Next Generation Control Icon Guide RD0046

description: The incoming AC line voltage is below the required operating level.
possible_causes: Low incoming line voltage; DC-bus or power-supply condition may also be involved when this alarm occurs with related power alarms.
official_corrective_action: Measure/compare the incoming and DC-bus voltage using the applicable Haas diagnostic procedure and inspect the power-supply/DC-bus system.
source_document: Haas 320V Power Supply Troubleshooting Guide; Haas Vector Drive Troubleshooting Guide

description: The REGEN load or associated power-supply system is reporting a short-circuit condition.
possible_causes: Problem with the REGEN load; shorted MMPS/power-supply condition.
official_corrective_action: Measure resistance across the REGEN load and inspect the MMPS/power-supply system using the Haas procedure.

description: The DC bus or associated power-supply system is reporting a short-circuit condition.
possible_causes: Problem with the DC bus; MMPS/power-supply short circuit.
official_corrective_action: Compare the measured DC voltage with the diagnostic page and inspect the MMPS for short circuits using the Haas service procedure.

description: The incoming AC line voltage is too high.
possible_causes: Incoming electrical supply overvoltage; related REGEN/DC-bus fault may also be present.
official_corrective_action: Measure incoming voltage and inspect the REGEN/DC-bus system when related alarms occur, following the applicable Haas power-supply troubleshooting procedure.
component: Incoming electrical power / DC bus / REGEN
source_document: Haas 320V Power Supply Troubleshooting Guide; REGEN Troubleshooting Guide

description: The DC bus voltage is above the allowable operating condition.
possible_causes: Problem with the REGEN load; faulty power-supply/MMPS condition.
official_corrective_action: Measure the resistance across the REGEN load and inspect the power-supply/MMPS system according to the Haas procedure.
source_document: Haas REGEN and 320V Power Supply Troubleshooting Guides

description: An X-axis serial encoder communication fault has been detected. Haas uses the digits before the decimal point to identify the axis in this alarm format.
possible_causes: Encoder communication problem in the X-axis feedback system; exact root cause requires the applicable Haas axis/encoder troubleshooting procedure.
official_corrective_action: Use the Haas alarm/axis troubleshooting documentation to diagnose the X-axis serial encoder communication path. Do not infer a failed encoder solely from the alarm number.
source_document: Haas Alarm Search Help Guide RD0002
